hook: Telangana HC asks why *13* warrants against MPs, MLAs are pending
hook_b: Telangana HC asks why *13* warrants against MPs, MLAs are pending
tldr: A Telangana High Court bench hearing a suo motu petition on cases against elected representatives questioned delays in executing NBWs and serving summons. It sought case-wise status and the oldest pending cases, and posted the matter to Nov 30.

beats.what: The High Court pulled up the state over unexecuted warrants in cases against MPs and MLAs.
beats.why: The bench said rising backlog could weaken public confidence in justice delivery.
beats.care: It suggested the approach used in lower courts: identify the oldest cases and dispose of them first.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 20): the bench wants chronological data on all pending cases up to March 31, 2026.

cards.q: Should cases against MPs and MLAs get time-bound trials?

qs: Why do summons go unserved despite technology?
Should MLCs also come under the special courts?

facts.t: Lower courts were told to identify the *30 oldest* cases in each district and dispose of at least 10.

viz.verdict: Most listed cases sit at the examination stage

learn.t: NBW = non-bailable warrant, a court order to arrest and produce a person

watch: The High Court hears the matter again on Nov 30.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Telangana high court pulls up state govt over 13 pending non-bailable warrants in cases against MPs, MLAs

fact: Non-bailable warrants are still unexecuted in *13* cases against Telangana MPs, MLAs
twist: Govt data showed 284 cases against MPs and MLAs as of April 2025, with only 15 disposed.
